rationale: States when the contract-labour Part applies and does not limit daily or weekly working hours.
Lets a court order a convicted employer to remedy the offence and does not limit working hours.
Lets a mine manager exceed ordinary hours of work in an emergency, which is an exception to the hours limits and not the limit itself.
Provides that no worker shall be required to work more than eight hours in a day, subject to notified intervals and spread-over.
Provides that no worker shall work more than six days in a week, which is the weekly rest limit rather than a weekly total of hours.
Bars persons who are deaf or who have defective vision from dangerous construction work and does not deal with women working at night.
Limits work to six days a week and does not say whether women may work at night.
States when the contract-labour Part applies and does not deal with night work by women.
Restricts contract labour in core activities and does not deal with women working night shifts.
Entitles women to all types of work and allows employment, with their consent, before 6 a.m. and after 7 p.m., subject to prescribed conditions on safety, holidays and working hours.

target: rules prescribing the safety, holiday and working-hour conditions for employing women before 6 a.m. or after 7 p.m. under osh-code-2020:43
rationale: Section 43 allows night work with consent but leaves the conditions the employer must observe to rules, which are not admitted.
Lets the owner reclaim wreck on paying salvage and does not compensate a seafarer for the loss of the ship.
Lets a receiver of wreck obtain a search warrant and does not provide seafarer compensation.
Appoints a receiver of wreck to take possession of wreck and does not pay the crew.
Requires the owner to provide free food and water to seafarers and is not compensation for loss of the vessel.
Lets undisbursed wage deposits be used for seafarer welfare after six years and is not compensation for a sinking.
Requires the owner to remove a wreck that is a hazard and does not indemnify the seafarers.
Requires the ship owner, if the vessel is lost or founders, to pay each seafarer onboard an indemnity against the resulting unemployment.

target: rules prescribing the unemployment indemnity payable to a seafarer on loss or foundering under merchant-shipping-2025:68
rationale: Section 68 creates the right to an indemnity but leaves its amount to rules, which are not admitted.
Allows an appeal if a court refuses to refer the parties to arbitration under section 54, which is the appeal and not the duty to refer.
Requires a court to refer the parties to arbitration where the agreement is one covered by section 44, unless it is void or inoperative, which is the foreign-award case and not every domestic clause.
Requires a court to refer the parties to arbitration where a contract covered by section 53 contains an arbitration agreement, which is another foreign-award chapter and not the general rule.
The general provision requiring a court to refer the parties to arbitration when the contract contains an arbitration agreement is not admitted.

Allows a thirty-day appeal against a Central Authority order and does not limit how long a complaint may take.
Lets the National Commission review its own order within thirty days and does not set the time for deciding the complaint.

Lets the District Commission review its own order within thirty days and does not set the time for deciding the complaint.
Requires the District Commission to decide a complaint as soon as possible and to endeavour to do so within three months, or five months where the goods need analysis or testing.

Punishes dealing in spurious goods and does not set the time for filing a consumer complaint.
Bars a ship owner from limiting liability for intentional or reckless loss, which is a different 'limitation' from the time for filing a complaint.
Punishes a false or misleading advertisement and does not set the time for filing a consumer complaint.

Lets a party apply to a Permanent Lok Adalat before going to court and does not set the time for a consumer complaint.
Punishes failure to comply with a commission's order and does not set the time for filing the complaint.
Provides that a consumer commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years of the cause of action, with a power to condone delay for sufficient cause.
Punishes manufacture or sale of spurious goods, which is not the punishment for a false or misleading advertisement.
Punishes dealing in adulterated products and does not punish a false advertisement.
Punishes a promoter who disobeys the Appellate Tribunal and does not punish a false advertisement.
